FACT_ID: sec13-R01 | anchor: A03
With sudden brake failure in an older vehicle, select a low gear and look for a place to stop. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec13-R02 | anchor: A03
For an older vehicle's failed brakes, pumping the pedal quickly may rebuild pressure. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec13-R03 | anchor: A03
If pumping fails, use the parking brake while holding its release so pressure can be eased if the rear wheels lock or skid. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec13-R04 | anchor: A03
If an older vehicle still cannot stop and a crash threatens, use ignition OFF as a last resort, never LOCK, then the lowest gear despite possible transmission damage. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec13-R05 | anchor: A03
After stopping for brake failure, call for help and do not continue driving. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec13-R06 | anchor: A03
Maintain tires and correct inflation to reduce blowout risk. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec13-R07 | anchor: A03
A front-tire blowout may shake the steering wheel and pull the vehicle sideways; rear-tire failure may drop a corner and make the rear wobble. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec13-R08 | anchor: A03
During a blowout, grip the wheel, ease off the accelerator and steer smoothly without abrupt large movements. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec13-R09 | anchor: A03
Avoid braking during a blowout; if braking is necessary, use gentle pressure while slowing to a safe off-road stop. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec13-R10 | anchor: A03
Continue on a flat tire only as needed to reach a safe place off the road before changing it. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec13-R11 | anchor: A03
Tire-changing steps vary by vehicle, so consult the owner's manual and retain the needed tools. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec13-R12 | anchor: A03
For the basic tire change, park on flat ground away from traffic and as far off the roadway as possible. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec13-R13 | anchor: A03
Set the parking brake and chock both the front and back of a remaining good tire. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec13-R14 | anchor: A03
If fitted, remove the hubcap or cover carefully before working on the wheel. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec13-R15 | anchor: A03
Loosen wheel nuts while the vehicle is still on the ground, without fully removing them. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec13-R16 | anchor: A03
Place the jack on solid ground at the manufacturer's proper frame or suspension point and raise the tire about six inches. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec13-R17 | anchor: A03
After raising the vehicle, remove and safely store the nuts, then pull the damaged wheel straight off with both hands. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec13-R18 | anchor: A03
Fit the spare and hand-thread every nut correctly before using only light wrench pressure. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec13-R19 | anchor: A03
Lower the vehicle slowly to the ground before final tightening, keeping the jack in place at that step. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec13-R20 | anchor: A03
Use the owner's manual for the correct wheel-nut tightening sequence and torque specification. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec13-R21 | anchor: A03
Stow the jack, wheel, tools and warning equipment securely after changing the tire. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec13-R22 | anchor: A03
Refit wheel covers or center caps as the manual directs and verify they are secure before driving. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec13-R23 | anchor: A04
For an oncoming vehicle in your lane, sound the horn and try a right-side escape if the other driver does not correct. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec13-R24 | anchor: A04
Do not evade a head-on threat by swerving left, because the opposing driver may return to that lane. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec13-R25 | anchor: A04
If a head-on collision cannot be avoided, brake firmly and steadily to reduce impact speed. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec13-R26 | anchor: A04
After the right wheels drop off pavement, ease off the accelerator and avoid abrupt braking or steering. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec13-R27 | anchor: A04
If braking is necessary to avoid a shoulder hazard, use gradual controlled pressure rather than locking the wheels. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec13-R28 | anchor: A04
With two wheels on and two off the road, hold the wheel firmly and steer parallel without scraping the pavement edge. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec13-R29 | anchor: A04
Before returning from a drop-off, slow below 25 mph, preferably near ten mph, with control restored. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec13-R30 | anchor: A04
Before reentry, check rear traffic and signal left; when clear, ease the right wheels onto pavement and steer gently right to straighten. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec13-R31 | anchor: A04
Match traffic speed only after safely regaining the pavement and full control. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec13-R32 | anchor: A04
Yield to a funeral procession and avoid cutting through it unless police or an authorized funeral representative directs otherwise. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec13-R33 | anchor: A04
Procession vehicles must show headlights, hazard flashers and a flag or identifying insignia; a purple warning light may also be used. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec13-R34 | anchor: A04
A funeral procession may follow its lead vehicle through a signal after the lead entered on green, or through a stop after the lead fully stopped. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec13-R35 | anchor: A04
Funeral processions must yield to emergency vehicles. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0068]
